A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IMPLIRET and provide readable main text, tables, figures, algorithms, and complete appendices. Content can be matched across pagination and table renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and oracle-RAG experiments in Tables 2–3, with additional retrieval results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 reports original retrieval and oracle-RAG results, adds GPT-o4-mini evaluation, and includes manual dataset validation and retrieval/generation error analyses.

M1.justification: The stated benchmark-generation components change: document synthesis switches from Llama 3.3-70B to Gemma-3-27B-it, and auxiliary lexical-resource generation switches from GPT-o1 to Gemma-3-27B-it. The tuple-generation algorithms, entity-binding and verification steps, and prompt templates remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions cover arithmetic, world knowledge, and temporal reasoning in English uni-speaker chats and multi-speaker forum posts. Table 1 retains 1,500 document-query pairs per category/style combination. The added audits and error analyses examine this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds GPT-o4-mini alongside the retained Llama 3.3-70B and GPT-4.1 readers. The six retrieval comparators in Table 2 remain BM25, ColBERT v2, Contriever, Dragon+, ReasonIR, and HippoRAG 2.

E3.justification: v3 adds a rank-stratified 72-passage manual audit and separate 60-query retrieval and generation error studies, with 120 evaluated generation cases. Appendix A.5 specifies sampling from ReasonIR's top-20 and bottom-20 ranks. Existing retrieval metrics and pool sizes remain; replacing 'All' with '30' in Table 3 clarifies the existing full-pool setting.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained category/style breakdowns and context-size comparison, v3 adds substantive checks of benchmark validity and failure mechanisms. The manual audit tests fluency, implicit support, and explicit leakage; Section 4 and new Tables 4–5 separately categorize retrieval misrankings and oracle-RAG generation errors.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed aggregation, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new audit sample counts and descriptive error percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Numerous retrieval values change in Table 2 and Appendix B: the leading average nDCG@10 changes from ReasonIR at 15.07 to Dragon+ at 14.91, while ReasonIR becomes 13.64. Table 3 retains the previous readers' scores and adds GPT-o4-mini averages of 92.74, 79.55, and 55.54 for k=1, 10, and 30. New outcomes include all 72 audited passages passing and the error distributions. The changed synthesis descriptions prevent treating retrieval revisions as established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The implicit-tuple definitions, uniqueness constraints, and mathematical construction rules are retained. Algorithms 1–3 match after accounting for formatting and placement. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a benchmark shifting reasoning from queries to implicit facts in documents, and the main claim remains that retrievers and long-context readers struggle with this setting. The abstract and conclusion update scores and the featured reader/context example as supporting evidence without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: The new error analysis offers heuristic explanations involving lexical overlap, topical cues, and passage length in retrieval, and malformed answers, non-answers, and distractor copying in generation. It interprets these patterns as reasons additional context alone is insufficient. The existing limitations concerning synthetic English data and shallow reasoning coverage remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 revises the documented synthesis-model identities, supplies the o4-mini-2025-04-16 checkpoint, and adds manual-evaluation sampling and assessment details in Appendix A.5. Existing construction algorithms, generation/evaluation prompts, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Gemma Team (2025) reference and removes the Meta (2024) Llama model-card and OpenAI (2024) o1 system-card references. Positioning relative to BEIR, RAR-b, BIRCO, BRIGHT, and query-side reasoning approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The overall section structure and most existing prose are retained. Local additions introduce the sanity check, error analysis, and Appendix A.5; smaller edits update result descriptions, correspondence information, and the arithmetic appendix reference from '2.1' to 'A.1'.

P2.justification: v3 adds two compact error-analysis tables and expands Table 3 with a GPT-o4-mini block. Existing appendix tables are renumbered and repositioned, and the detailed-results caption is revised. Figures 1–17 and their substantive visual content are retained, with limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 supplements v1's automatic validation and aggregate evaluations with manual checks of benchmark quality and explicit failure analyses, improving evidential support and interpretability. The additional reader also broadens the empirical assessment. The gains remain limited by small heuristic samples, the unspecified reader in the generation-error analysis, and the unexplained relationship between changed synthesis models and revised retrieval scores.
